haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices only to the shadow store, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person then approves the move, and the controller writes billing_mode.
haiku-low.q4: New-engine charge failures above 2% in any 10-minute window start an automatic rollback, but only in both or new_only. Shadow errors never trigger it.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gates reset. Step 5 must finish first, then a person must approve the move to shadow before the new engine advances.
haiku-low.q6: After day 35 in new_only. The usage event log expires skipped events by then, so catch-up cannot finish from events. The brief defines no path; on-call decides.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode before each charge and never cache it for a run. The document does not say how workers are notified or what happens to an in-progress invoice.
haiku-low.q8: In the rollout record and audit log, including approval and Finance sign-off references. Only the controller writes billing_mode, and forward moves need a recorded person approval.
haiku-low.q9: The rollout controller measures new-engine charge failures over 10-minute windows. When above 2%, it starts an automatic rollback, setting the freeze marker.
haiku-low.q10: During steps 1 to 4 they are not charged and wait for step 5. Step 5 charges due-list invoices after every worker reads old_only, before normal runs.
haiku-low.q11: Shared idempotency keys block duplicate charges at provider and ledger. Step 3 records successes so the old engine skips them; unknown charges are resolved by key, never retried under a new key.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays on the rollback path with the freeze marker set, due charges queued. The failed step resumes on retry until step 5 finishes.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store only (never charged, never written to the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current for rollback.
sonnet.q3: Gate: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person approves the move; the controller then writes billing_mode.
sonnet.q4: Automatic start when new-engine charge failures exceed 2% over any 10-minute window, only in both or new_only (new_only only before day 35). Shadow errors never trigger it.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with the gates reset. The new engine cannot take over until a person approves the move to shadow, then the gates must be met again (7-day shadow count starts at shadow entry), then both, then new_only.
sonnet.q6: At day 35 (35 days after entry into new_only), when the oldest skipped usage event leaves the 35-day usage event log, so catch-up from events is no longer possible. After day 35 the document defines no path; the controller pages on-call and waits for a person's decision.
sonnet.q7: Engines read billing_mode from the config service before each charge and never cache it for a run. NOT STATED for how an invoice already being processed at the moment of the flip is handled, beyond the idempotency key (same key for a period; provider and ledger refuse a second charge) guarding against overlap.
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED as a single place for evidence. The rollout record holds the shadow streak and invoice count, unresolved mismatch count, Finance sign-off reference and approval references; changes go to the audit log. Nothing stops promotion except that forward moves need a person's recorded approval when the gate is met, one step at a time; how the gate is enforced is not stated (the approval tool is an open question).
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller. It watches new-engine charge failures (failures above 2% over any 10-minute window; the exact denominator and minimum count are open). When met it starts an automatic rollback (sets the freeze marker and runs steps 1 to 5).
sonnet.q10: They are not charged during steps 1 to 4; they wait. They are charged in step 5 by the old engine, after billing_mode is set to old_only, every worker reads old_only, and the freeze marker is cleared, from the due list under the same ledger invoice version and idempotency key, before the old engine's normal run. No limit on the wait is set.
sonnet.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing period, invoice version): the provider and ledger refuse a second charge with the same key. Also step 2 resolves unknown charges by key, step 3 writes successes to the ledger charge record, the old engine skips any period with a charge record, and the due list only contains invoices with no charge record.
sonnet.q12: The rollout stays on the rollback path and does not move forward; due charges stay queued, and the freeze marker remains for both/new_only so nothing new charges. Each step is idempotent and resumable, so the failed step resumes on retry.
